result.label: Function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on ' and' or ',' joining a list of beneficial outcomes after a verb phrase like "improves efficiency", where the next item is likely a result verb such as "reducing", "increasing" or "improving". Silent on plain noun-list conjunctions.
result.label: Comma/and in benefit-outcome lists

result.description: Fires on a comma ending a long introductory clause or phrase about broad topics (globalization, technology, climate), where a new main clause with a subject (the, it, many, countries) comes next. Silent on commas inside lists.
result.label: Comma after introductory clause

result.description: Fires on '&' in abbreviations like M&A, and on items in lists of business-analysis terms such as PEST/PESTEL (Political, Economic, Social). Mixed peaks, with weak firing on some function words; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: '&' in M&A and PEST lists

result.description: Fires on scattered adverb-like or modifier tokens such as " otherwise", "-ally", " previously", and verbs like "started" or "combine". They often follow "that" or sit before an adjective or participle. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is a weak fit.
result.label: Mixed adverbs: otherwise, -ally, previously

result.description: Fires on mixed connective and function words (' and', ' like', ' to', commas) in abstract expository prose, where the next word continues an abstract noun or adjective phrase. It is silent on ' and' ending a comma list. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Connectives in abstract expository prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' mob' when it begins "mobility" (ion/electron/labor mobility), predicting "ility". Silent when "mobility" starts the text with no preceding context.
result.label: ' mob' piece of "mobility"

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: the suffix 'ist' in -ist/-ism words (absolutist, nativist), 'in' after "warm weather conditions", and other mid-phrase words. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak. Contrast 'colonist' is silent.
result.label: Scattered 'ist' suffix and 'in' tokens

result.description: Fires on modal verbs, mostly ' will' (also ' to', ' should', 'll'), after an abstract or technology subject in forward-looking text about future developments. Predicts a verb like 'begin', 'advance' or 'yield'. Silent on some ' will' contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Future modal 'will' after tech subject

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after "zero" (as in "zero-sum"), and weakly on similar prefix pieces. It stays silent on hyphens after other words like "mid-", "decision-", "long-".
result.label: Hyphen after "zero"

result.description: Fires on verb endings or words like facilitate, foster(s), reinforces, and "for effective" in essays about communication, where a positive outcome noun is expected next (e.g., discussion, culture). Mixed peaks; weak consistency.
result.label: Fostering/facilitating verbs in communication text

result.description: Fires on the first name " Charles" when it starts a person's name, especially in lists of scholars or scientists (e.g. "like Charles K.", "Charles Sanders Peirce"). It is silent on the contrast list of names. Likely predicts a surname next.
result.label: Charles as first name

result.description: Fires on " Social"/" social" right after "Corporate" in "Corporate Social Responsibility" (mostly capitalized). Silent on plain "corporate governance" text without the word social. Members detect "social" and corporate-business context.
result.label: Corporate Social (Responsibility)

result.description: Fires on ' word'/' words' (or 'term') right after a language-origin phrase like "comes from the Greek", introducing a quoted foreign etymon. Silent on 'word' in other uses.
result.label: Etymology 'Greek word' noun

result.description: Fires on 'ull' in "hull" mid-word and on assorted noun/word pieces ending a title or compound term (World Market, network, user, immersion). Silent on 'ull' at document start. Mixed evidence.
result.label: 'ull' in hull, plus scattered noun pieces

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece 'att' inside words like lattices, watt, unattainable, attitudes, with weaker firing on some commas and ' At'. Members are 'att' detectors; the output pushes toward word continuations such as 'ices'.
result.label: 'att' word-piece (lattices, watt)

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Brun' (Brunelleschi) and also on scattered mid-word or noun-modifier pieces like 'ch' in chordal, ' fuel', ' and'. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so the story is unclear.
result.label: Brun(elleschi) and scattered word pieces

result.description: Fires mostly on ' are' (also 'ologies', 'see', ' their') after a plural technical subject such as systems, techniques or processes in expository text, where a predicate like "often/typically/integral" is expected. Silent on some ' are' in other clauses.
result.label: Plural-subject 'are' in technical prose

result.description: Fires on function words (as, through, with, via, share, to) linking a verb or noun to a following object in chemistry-flavored text about reactants, phases and shared interactions. Silent on 'as' in other uses like "such as" or "as well as".
result.label: Function words in reactant/sharing chemistry text

result.description: Fires on function words (with, to, from, regional) in essays about language, writing systems and ancient cultural influence, where one script or culture is mixed with or evolved from another. Silent on 'with' in other constructions. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Influence/evolution prepositions in language history

result.description: Fires on the token " weak", mainly in physics (weak nuclear force) and also in chemistry (weak bases) and "weak points". Members include detectors of " weak" and of " strong". Silent on the contrast text, which has no " weak".
result.label: " weak" token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on the hyphen in "fine-" (fine-tuning), also on a few other tokens like " Cultural" and " as". Silent on hyphens in other compounds (ultra-, out-of-bag), so it seems tied to the "fine-" prefix.
result.label: Hyphen in "fine-tuning"

result.description: Fires on the verb ' began' (also started/begin) right after an abstract or plural subject noun, typically before "to + verb" describing a process or trend starting to emerge. Silent in at least one case of "began to take place".
result.label: "began" after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' merc' when it begins "mercantilism/mercantile/merchant", before the rest of the word is spelled out. Members mostly detect other incomplete word-start fragments (agricult, mort, Protest).
result.label: ' merc' word-start (mercantilism)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and commas (",", " and", " or", " the") in abstract expository text about communication or measurement. The contrast shows it silent on commas after list items. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' and', ' a', ' of', ' each', ' final', ' not', ' including') in expository text, mid-sentence where a noun phrase or list item is expected next. No dominant token and no clear condition; the members are diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on mixed function-word tokens (apostrophe after plural "Years'", " and", " as" in "such as", " or", " static") in expository text, where a noun or modifier is expected next. The circuit is diffuse and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Mixed connective tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' st' when it begins a longer word, most strongly in "striving/strive" after a subject and adverb (e.g. "still striving"). Weaker on "stakeholder" and "starring". It predicts continuations like "riv".
result.label: ' st' start of "striving"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fost' as the start of "foster", usually after "can" or "to" with a subject that promotes something. It stays quiet in some cases where "fostering" or "fosters" starts a clause.
result.label: ' fost' in foster (verb)

result.description: Fires on the piece "une" in "imm|une", mainly when followed by "system" or "system's" in the windows. It is silent on "imm|une" before "response" or "cells", so it seems to need a system-type continuation.
result.label: imm-une before "system"

result.description: Fires on ' principle' when it starts a sentence right after a full stop, as the subject of a new sentence (e.g. "principle of conservation of…"). It stays quiet when 'principle' follows an adjective or determiner such as "fundamental" or "this".
result.label: Sentence-initial ' principle'

result.description: Fires on adjective-ending suffixes (-ive, -ic, -ative, -ble, -ous, -al) or adjectives like "fine" and "right" that end an item in a list of adjective types or categories, e.g. "coarse, medium or fine". Silent on the same suffixes in other contexts.
result.label: Adjective suffix in type lists

result.description: Fires on verbs like "is", "are", "have", "operate" right after a subject in economics definitions of efficiency or equilibrium (e.g. "where production is", "firms operate"). It stays quiet on "is" in cooking or other non-economic text.
result.label: Copular verbs in economics definitions

result.description: Fires most often on the word piece ' prov' (prove/provisions) but also on scattered function words and commas in explanatory academic text. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: ' prov' plus scattered function words
'lor' inside chlor- words
result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'lor' after 'ch' in chemistry words like chloride, chlorophyll, chloroplast. It stays silent when 'lor' starts a word (lorophyll). Weak activity on a few scattered tokens in chemistry text.

Fires on function words and connectors (and, to, on, for, commas) that continue a list or verb phrase in abstract expository text describing what a process or field "involves". Contrast shows it is silent on some 'and' joining nouns.
result.label: Connectors in 'involves…' expository lists

result.description: Fires mostly on a bare 't' token (apostrophe-t, as in "'t" after a stripped negation stem) and sometimes on ' and', 's', ' any'. Silent on ordinary "n't" contractions like "isn't", "don't". Members detect 't' and 'not' tokens. Weak and mixed.
result.label: Stray 't' after apostrophe, not n't

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Th" (also " in") when a word like Thermodynamics or Theme is being started, mostly after "Law of". Predicts continuations such as "erm". Silent on ordinary running text.
result.label: " Th" word-start, Thermodynamics

result.description: Fires on "to" (or "in") right after causal verbs like "leading", "led", "resulting", where a consequence follows. Silent on other uses of "to" such as "extends to" or "approach to". Predicts outcome words like increased, improved, greater.
result.label: Causal "leading to / resulting in"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' green' (greenhouse, greenery, green chemistry, green marketing), mostly in environmental text, as a prefix-like word predicting continuations such as 'house' or 'ery'. Members are mainly green/color detectors.
result.label: ' green' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " im" that begins "imputation"/"imputed" in statistics text about missing data. Members are mostly " im" prefix detectors. Weak elsewhere (" settlement", "sch").
result.label: " im" start of imputation

result.description: Fires on enabling/allowing words (' for' after "allows", "enabling", "instantaneous", "enables") in tech or traffic text about real-time feedback and data. It stays silent on "allows for" in generic improvement or efficiency contexts.
result.label: Enabling words in real-time traffic feedback

result.description: Fires mostly on word-fragment tokens, especially 'ust' at the start of "Sustainable/Sustainability", plus 'ques' and some hyphens or mid-word pieces. It seems to predict a word continuation. Mixed evidence, weak faithfulness.
result.label: Word-start fragments, 'Sust' in Sustainable

result.description: Fires on ' property' (also ownership, land) in economics/legal text about property rights and ownership. It stays silent when 'property' follows 'intellectual', so it needs the physical or economic sense, not the IP sense.
result.label: Property (not intellectual) in economics

result.description: Fires mainly on commas separating items in a list of abstract nouns (traditions, customs, arts, languages), plus a few word pieces like 'ically' and ' V'. Silent on commas after clauses or introductory phrases.
result.label: Commas in noun lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (commas, "to", "of", " natural", "ye") in passages about dyes, materials and crafts. It seems to predict word continuations like "-les" or "-le". Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered tokens in dye/material text

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "or" in lists of abstract nouns (ideas, feelings, thoughts) in texts about communication, right after the first list item. Silent on similar commas in other lists and topics.
result.label: List separators in communication text

result.description: Fires on example-introducing words (' like', 'such as', 'including', 'include') that follow text about collaboration and communication tools, just before a list of examples such as shared workspaces. Silent on 'like' in other topics such as applications and monitoring.
result.label: Examples intro in collaboration text

result.description: Fires on mid-compound pieces where a word continues: the hyphen in "on-the-go"/"on-the-move" and "stal" in "crystal" followed by "lattice". Silent on "Crystal" at document start. Mixed and weakly consistent.
result.label: Hyphen in on-the-go; crystal 'stal'

result.description: Fires on an apostrophe that begins a contraction ('s, 'll, 're) right after a sentence-ending period, where "It" or "They" seems to be missing. It stays silent on apostrophes inside words, such as possessives and "don't".
result.label: Apostrophe after period starting contraction

result.description: Fires on ' the' / ' The' when it begins a new sentence or heading, often after a period with no capital (e.g. ".[[ the]] 19…"). It stays silent on mid-sentence ' the' after verbs or prepositions.
result.label: Sentence-initial 'the' after period

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' of', also ' by', ' involve', ' the') right after a subject noun in definitional passages about economic cycles. Silent on many other ' of' tokens, so the pattern is topic-bound and only loosely consistent.
result.label: Function words in economic-cycle definitions

result.description: Fires on " new" as an adjective after verbs like explore, seek, or open to, mostly in creative or artistic text. It predicts a following noun such as ideas, sounds or techniques. Weakly fires on "innovative".
result.label: " new" after explore/seek verbs

result.description: Fires on varied word-start or word-piece tokens (e.g. '1' in "greater than 1", 'W' in acronyms, ' n', 'RA' in RAID) where the word is incomplete or a short symbol, often in math or acronym contexts. Silent on '1' in dates and headings.
result.label: Word-start pieces, math symbols, acronyms

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'igen', mostly in "indigenous" (also in antigen, eigenvalues), after a preceding 'ind'/'ant'/'E' piece. Members are mostly 'igen' detectors plus 'ind-' prefix pieces.
result.label: 'igen' word piece (indigenous)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "quest" inside "sequestration", mostly in carbon sequestration text. Members detect "quest" and other mid-word pieces. The contrast has no "quest" token.
result.label: "quest" in sequestration

result.description: Fires on the end of an action noun (manipulation, visualization, exchange, distribution, retrieval, transfer) after "easy/efficient/real-time" or "data" in software or tech descriptions. Silent on "manipulation" in other settings (array manipulation, modulation).
result.label: Process noun after easy/data in tech text

result.description: Fires on commas, "through", apostrophes and similar function tokens in text about early or ancient origins (early bilaterians, nervous systems, prehistoric writing). Seems to anticipate historical or developmental continuation; silent on commas in other historical passages.
result.label: Function tokens in early-origins history text

result.description: Fires on connective words like " but", " where", " with", "who" that extend an analogy or simile in explanatory text (e.g., sets as clubs/bouncers, puzzles "but with added..."). Silent on "not just X, but also" constructions.
result.label: Connectives extending analogies

result.description: Fires mostly on " memory" in computer-science text about memory management, allocation and hierarchy, as the head noun after words like virtual, physical, or efficient. It stays quiet in "execution time and memory usage" and "main memory hierarchy".
result.label: memory in computing/memory management

result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "work-life" (e.g. work-life balance), after "work". It stays quiet on hyphens in other compounds such as AI-based or long-term. Many members detect hyphens generally, others detect "work".
result.label: Hyphen in work-life

result.description: Fires on 'zone'/'zones' (and 'longitude', 'lines') in time-zone and geography text, especially after 'time' or 'hour'. Weaker firing on word endings like 'ories' and 'ems'. Members are mostly diffuse context features.
result.label: time zone / longitude geography words

result.description: Fires on function words (to, of, as, in, improved) in generic text about manufacturing/engineering benefits, where the next word would be a production-related noun (assembly, operator, production). Silent on ' to' in business/abstract text.
result.label: Function words in manufacturing benefit text

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' prof' in "profound", ' in', commas) in essay-like academic text, especially about religious symbols and abstract meaning. Often silent on ' in' elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Mixed tokens in symbolism essays

result.description: Fires mostly on commas inside long lists of parallel items (e.g. reflexive pronouns "herself, itself, ourselves,"), and sometimes on "such as" or "to" introducing examples. Silent on commas after an introductory phrase or clause.
result.label: Commas within enumerated lists

result.description: Fires on plural economic nouns (prices, wages, markets, rates, services) as the subject of an economics passage, especially in factor-market or price-setting explanations. Silent on 'markets' inside prepositional phrases such as 'financial markets'.
result.label: Plural economic subject nouns (prices, wages)

result.description: Fires on ' its' (occasionally ' their') right after a sentence-opening preposition like "With its" or "Despite its", where a descriptive noun such as "rich history" follows. Silent on 'its' after mid-sentence "due to" or "for".
result.label: Sentence-initial "With its" possessive

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ('als' in metals lists, ' of', commas, ' like') in technical or science passages, within enumerations of examples or classifications. Silent on 'als' in other words like integrals. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Mixed tokens in science enumerations

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verb pieces (of, which, with, -ating, both) inside technical expository text on math, computing and logic. Peak tokens are scattered, and the target is silent on some of its own peak tokens, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Technical text function words, mixed

result.description: Fires on a comma ending a clause about interdisciplinary or academic integration (fields, disciplines, laws), where a participial or elaborating phrase follows (fostering, inspiring, as well as, with). Silent on commas in other academic text.
result.label: Comma after interdisciplinary integration clause

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' Trade', 'iff' in tariff, ' and', ' on, ' average') mostly in economics/trade and academic text. Stays silent on ' Trade' in fixed names like World Trade Organization. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered economics/trade tokens

result.description: Fires on " how" introducing a clause after study/understanding verbs in academic text (e.g. "the study of how", "examining how", "insights into how"). Silent on some " how" uses in other contexts, such as "exploring how" in an art/interdisciplinary passage.
result.label: "how" after study/understand phrases

result.description: Fires on varied word-ending pieces (-ated, -ises, -ed, -ured, -ation) and on ' equilibrium' in chemistry-like text, but is silent on some ' equilibrium' tokens. Mixed, low-consistency peaks with no clear shared role.
result.label: Mixed suffix pieces and 'equilibrium'

result.description: Fires on varied function words and abstract nouns (desire, quest, and, the, an) in art-criticism prose, where a noun like "desire for" or "possibilities" is expected next. Members are mostly art/artist-themed context. Mixed peaks, low consistency.
result.label: Art-writing abstract noun/function slots

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'son' piece inside "consonance"/"consonantal" in linguistics and phonetics text. It stays silent on 'son' in surnames like Erikson or Jakobson. It also fires weakly on scattered words such as ' various' and ' as'.
result.label: 'son' in consonant words

result.description: Fires on varied connective tokens (' through', ' and', ' track', commas) in generic text about creative techniques, such as audio and music segmentation or literary mixing. It is silent on ' through' in other creative-expression phrases. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Connectives in creative technique lists
' not' after auxiliary verb (not only)
result.description: Fires on ' not' directly after an auxiliary like has/had/were/may, especially in "has not only", "not just", "not always" patterns. Members are ' not' detectors that push toward only/just/necessarily/always. Silent on 'not' in other positions, e.g. after "are" in relative clauses.

Fires on plural-noun-like tokens about characters or relationships (' characters', 'acters', 'ationships', ' populations') in abstract essay-style text about people and stories. It is silent on ' characters' in many other contexts, and the reason is unclear.
result.label: Plural 'characters' and relationships nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also commas in number lists, ' and') mid-sentence in linguistics and academic prose, where the next word is likely an abstract noun like "understanding" or "unique". It is silent on many other ' the' tokens, and the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' the' before abstract noun, linguistics

result.description: Fires on function words (' of', ' and', ' the', ' be') and some nouns in abstract academic prose about linguistics, structures and systems. It is silent on the same ' of' in similar morphology text, so the evidence is mixed and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (closing parenthesis, pieces of "laser", "strand", "multipotency") in science text, mostly physics and biology. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse and failed. Specific triggers are unclear.
result.label: Scattered science-text tokens, diffuse

result.description: Fires on the ending of physics field names, mainly "ics" in "Mechanics" and " Theory", in lists of academic topics. It stays silent on "ics" in other words like Aesthetics, Dynamics, Infographics and Plastics.
result.label: Physics field name endings (Mechanics)

result.description: Fires on ' the' (rarely ' a'/' its') right after verbs of exceeding or surpassing, like "exceed the", "surpasses the", "exceeds a", in physics-threshold text. It stays silent on ' the' after verbs like "understanding" or "defines".
result.label: 'the' after exceed/surpass

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'icul' mainly inside "meticulous(ly)", also in "curriculum". Members are detectors of 'icul' and similar mid-word pieces that continue into -ous/-ously. It stays silent on some 'meticulously' cases.
result.label: 'icul' in meticulous

result.description: Fires on possessive determiners (my, your, his, her, our) mostly when they are listed or discussed in grammar text about possessive forms. It also fires on ordinary 'my' before a noun. Predicts kin or relational nouns next.
result.label: Possessive determiners (my, your, his)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (commas, 'of', 'as', 'that', 'od') in expository, explanatory text about science or English grammar. No dominant token, and the logits are mixed. The evidence is weak and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks in expository text

result.description: Fires on connecting words (' of', ' and', 'merges') in text about musical theatre and music, where the next word continues a music/theatre phrase. It stays silent on ' and' in other topics such as transport, governance and code.
result.label: Connector words in musical theatre text

result.description: Fires on varied function words (and, that, a, of, '.') inside passages about fiscal and economic policy, where upstream members signal economics/government context. It is silent on the same '.' in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in fiscal-policy text

result.description: Fires on a modifier noun or word piece inside a compound noun phrase after "a/an" in analogies or descriptions (ball|room, story|telling, love story, text|book, comedy club). It predicts the head noun that completes the compound.
result.label: Compound-noun first part in analogies

result.description: Fires mostly on hyphens joining name or compound parts (Sapir-Whorf, Ford-Fulkerson), plus scattered tokens like ' food', ' aqu', ' the' in technical text. Silent on some hyphens (first-, codon-), so the pattern is mixed and the condition unclear.
result.label: Hyphen in name compounds, mixed

result.description: Fires diffuse across mixed positions (commas, 'the', word pieces, 'processing') in technical or academic text. It pushes against conjunction-like next words (when, while, before, only). The evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Diffuse mixed tokens in technical text

result.description: Fires on scattered, unrelated tokens (commas, ' of', 'sin', 'ord', word pieces) with no clear shared pattern. It is silent on most commas, and the members are diffuse, so the circuit is poorly explained.
result.label: Scattered mixed tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on the final piece of technical physics/engineering terms, mostly 'ator' completing "Stellarator", also 'on' and similar endings in plasma/fusion text. Silent on 'ator' in unrelated words like "instabilitator".
result.label: Stellarator word-ending piece

result.description: Fires on the word " binary" (also "Binary"), mostly as a modifier before nouns like trees, search, operations, logic or fission. Members are binary-token detectors. It was silent on one document-initial " binary" example, so the extra condition is unclear.
result.label: binary token detector

result.description: Fires on the word fragment " sympt" (start of "symptoms"), usually in health or psychological text. Members detect other split-word beginnings (dise-, ris-, inj-, bar-) that precede a completion like "-oms" or "-ases".
result.label: " sympt" word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (navigate, within, in, by, how, the) in abstract academic text about relationships, communication and theory, where a noun phrase on tensions or processes is expected next. Peaks are scattered, and the contrast text is narrative fiction.
result.label: Academic relational-theory function words

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'om' in the middle of longer words, mostly 'on|om|atopoeia' and also cohomology, biomarker, clinometers. Silent on 'om' at the start of a word like 'omatopusop'.
result.label: 'om' inside onomatopoeia-like words

result.description: Fires mostly on ' back' in "more than just a back|drop" (setting as backdrop), also ' watch' and a few other word-start pieces. It is silent on 'backdrop' after adjectives or plural uses. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: 'back' in "just a backdrop"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verb pieces (' for', ' under', ' of', ' carried', ' want') in expository text, often cooking or science, where a preposition or complement is expected. Peak tokens are varied and the circuit is diffuse and weak.
result.label: Diffuse function words in cooking/science text

result.description: Fires on the word "role" (and "Ro|le") as the head noun of a "The (adj) role of X" title-like phrase, often at document start in economics, tech or religion text. It stays silent on "play an important role in" in environmental or biology text.
result.label: "The role of…" noun phrase

result.description: Fires on word-start or mid-word pieces (' Jeff', ' Fitz', ' nost', Cyrillic 'ово') in list-like text of short items, such as names or terms one per line. Weak, mixed evidence; the logits are not coherent.
result.label: Name/word pieces in line lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cor' when it begins "coral" (e.g. "coral bleaching"), in coral/reef text. Members mostly detect ' cor' itself, including its "corrosion" use. The contrast suggests it needs the coral-style continuation or context.
result.label: ' cor' piece in coral

result.description: Fires on words for political self-rule or liberation (independence, freedom, autonomy, self-determination, liberation) in text about colonial or national struggles. It stays silent on the decolonization passage about Vietnam, so it needs the sought-after-freedom framing.
result.label: Independence/freedom in anti-colonial context

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (that, the, of, ed, Robert) inside linguistics-themed text, such as language identity and vowel shifts. Members mostly push language-related next words. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on the final suffix piece of an abstract noun (existence, isolation, urgency, simplicity) when it ends a topic-title or concept-list entry, such as in lists of philosophy or academic subjects. Silent on concrete-topic lists.
result.label: Abstract noun endings in topic lists

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and tokens (y, through, sea, plastic, tree, cular) in the middle of a noun phrase or modifier, mostly after "not just/not only" style contrasts. Weakly pushes toward plural nouns like attempts, forms, models. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed mid-phrase word pieces, noun-ish

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (' in', ' for', ' to', '-', ' through') that follow a verb or noun and introduce a complement, e.g. "competing for power". Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered prepositions after predicates

result.description: Fires on a few specific tokens: the '+' in "B+ trees" or chemical/symbol strings, and ' tong' in "tongs" (kitchen tools). Also weakly on ' que' in "queues". Mixed, token-specific pieces rather than one theme.
result.label: '+' and 'tong(s)' token pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ',', ' of', ' by') mid-phrase in linguistics/language-development text, predicting a following continuation like ',' or 'which'. Silent on 'and' closing lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in linguistics prose

result.description: Fires on word-piece 'in' (and 'ize') inside a word or hyphenated compound where a continuation is expected, e.g. mar-in-ade, well-in-formed, familiar-ize. Silent on 'in' inside other words like distinctions or reminiscent.
result.label: 'in'/'ize' mid-word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' of', ' not', 'ing', ' oil', ' out') in text about risk management and oil recovery, where a verb or process noun is expected. It stays silent on many ' of' tokens elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Risk/oil process text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the verb right after "not only" (provides, demonstrates, facilitate, reflects, safeguard), where "but also" is expected next. Silent on the same word pieces like "es" elsewhere. Members detect "not only/more than just" frames and "but".
result.label: Verb after "not only"

result.description: Fires on ' the' (or 's) right after an opening phrase like "Throughout history," at the start of a document, before a subject such as "tale/use of humanity". It stays silent on ' the' in other mid-text spots.
result.label: 'the' after opening "Throughout history,"

result.description: Fires on 'ass' in "brass" (musical instruments) and on a document-initial " When". Silent on 'ass' in bluegrass, encompasses, or a bare initial 'ass'. Members detect 'ass' and instrument words.
result.label: 'ass' in brass; opening 'When'

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' vol' (volcano, volatile) and 'ch' (game-changer, chord, synchrotron), where a longer word is continued in the next token. Mixed, weakly consistent peaks; the strongest context is 'ch' in "game-changer".
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments vol/ch

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and list/connector tokens (commas, "and", "including", "compar-" pieces) mid-sentence in expository text, where a noun or category item comes next. Peaks are mixed; evidence is weak and the circuit failed.
result.label: Mixed connectors before noun continuation

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase tokens in abstract expository text (e.g. 'ological' in geological/biological, 'their', 'world', 'current', 'highlight'). No single token dominates; the peaks are inconsistent and it stays silent on some of the same tokens, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tant' when it starts a longer word, mainly 'tantamount' (also tantalize, tantalism, tantrums). Members mostly detect incomplete word-start fragments such as ' tant', ' inten', ' cor' and ' oscill'.
result.label: ' tant' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on a comma or "and" joining coordinated adjectives (personal, professional, educational), right after an adjective like "personal" or "professional". It likely predicts another such adjective (e.g. " professional"). It stays quiet on commas joining other clause types.
result.label: Comma/and between coordinated setting adjectives

result.description: Fires on function words (that, of, the, and, as, with, by) in music/brain/health science text, where the next word is likely a topic term such as music or neural. Silent on relative-clause "that" after a noun like "mechanisms that".
result.label: Function words in music-science text

result.description: Fires on ' hold' as the piece completing "stakehold(ers)", in business/project-management text. It stays silent on the same piece in "sharehold(ers)", so it needs the "stake" prefix.
result.label: hold in "stakeholders"

result.description: Fires on word pieces in biology/biochemistry text, such as 'ili' in pili, 'om' in chromosomal and 'ic' in organometallic. It stays quiet on 'om' in non-biological words like boom and atomizer. Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are scattered.
result.label: Biology word-piece fragments (pili, chromosomal)

result.description: Fires on " careful" (and "meticul-ous") as a modifier of an upcoming noun, mostly after "requires" or similar, in expository text about work needing care. It predicts nouns like planning, consideration and selection.
result.label: careful/meticulous before process noun

result.description: Fires on hyphen or en-dash (also soft hyphen) in the second hyphen of word-order terms like Subject-Verb-Object, where the next piece is a continuation. Silent on hyphens in other compounds like employee-friendly or tree-like.
result.label: Hyphen in Subject-Verb-Object terms

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' trans' split off at the start of a longer word, mainly in "phase transitions" (before -itions/-itional). Predicts suffixes like 'itions'. Silent on other words, such as thermal.
result.label: ' trans' in "phase transitions"

result.description: Fires on function words (of, to, the, reflected) in text about colonialism, independence and decolonization, where the next word is likely colonial or administrative. It stays silent on 'of' in other topics such as trade, industry or culture.
result.label: Function words in colonial/decolonization text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, most often the piece "vent" in "unconventional", plus "level" in "sea-level", " the", " traditional", " section". No single token or context dominates, and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Scattered tokens, mostly 'vent'

result.description: Fires on function words or word pieces (perpet-"uate", "by", "to", "on") right before a likely inequality or disparity term, in texts about social inequality, race, gender, and socioeconomic status. Logits favor "dispar" and "sympt".
result.label: Inequality-context connector before disparity terms
'the' after identify/define verbs
result.description: Fires on ' the' (occasionally possessive 's) right after a transitive verb like identify, define, map out, outline, in business-process writing, where a noun like factors, structure or dynamics is expected. Silent on 'the' after prepositions.

Fires on " Background" as the last word of "Cosmic Microwave Background" (or Neutrino Background) in cosmology text. Silent on "Background" as a section heading, so it needs the cosmic-background phrase.
result.label: Cosmic Microwave Background token

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ',', ' on', ' from', ' of', mid-word fragments) in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent, the contrast silences ' and' in lists, and the circuit is diffuse and unreliable.
result.label: Diffuse function-word and fragment firing

result.description: Fires on the word " email" (also " Email"), mostly as a modifier or topic in phrases like "email communication". Members are mainly email detectors from earlier layers. Weaker on "emails" and "mail"; silent on general messaging text without the word.
result.label: Word 'email' detector

result.description: Fires on the word " without" (rarely " no" or " little") when it introduces a clause about something absent, often right before "any". Members are mostly " without" detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: ' without' preposition detector

result.description: Fires on the word that takes an object in understanding/comprehension phrases: "compreh-end", "understand", "understanding", "grasp of", "knowledge of", expecting a following topic noun phrase. Silent on 'end' inside other words like "interdependence" or "ascend".
result.label: Understanding/comprehending verbs before object

result.description: Fires on function words (to, that, they, can) and 'continu-ously' in tech/UI text about user interaction and adaptive systems, where a verb is expected next (e.g. continue, update). Silent on 'to' in other analysis contexts. Upstream members are largely user/UI detectors.
result.label: Function words in user-interface/adaptive-tech text
Commas/function words in physics lists
result.description: Fires on commas and some function words (a, that, the, represents) mid-sentence in technical explanatory text, mostly quantum physics or abstract concepts, where a list item or clause continues. Silent on many commas in similar science text.

Fires mostly on sentence-initial additive transitions like " Additionally", " Furthermore", " Moreover" at the start of a text or paragraph; weaker, scattered firing on " the", " and", " or". Logits are not clear.
result.label: Additive transition words (Furthermore/Additionally)

result.description: Fires on the start of a word fragment (' col', ' n', ' et', ' d') in grammar and linguistics text, such as "collocation", "noun" or "dative", where a technical term is being spelled out. It stays silent on "colloquial".
result.label: Linguistics term word-start fragments

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also commas, 'nes', 'ut') right after a colon or comma that introduces a list of components or parts, as in "three parts: the major premise, the minor premise", in academic and technical explanations. Silent on ' the' in culinary text.
result.label: 'the' in lists of components

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (have, with, to, has, about, create, present) that follow a subject in abstract economics/policy prose, where a consequence or effect is about to be stated. Silent on 'about' after 'concern' or 'discussions'.
result.label: Effect-introducing verbs in economics prose

result.description: Fires on importance adjectives (' important', ' prominent', 'cial', ' significant') after "becoming increasingly/more" or "play a", in sustainability/technology trend prose. Silent on "it is important that".
result.label: Increasingly important (trend adjective)

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (in, of, to, shapes, defines) after a subject in text about fiction, worldbuilding and storytelling. It predicts story-related nouns like characters, conflict and protagonist next. Peaks are mixed across tokens.
result.label: Function words in storytelling/worldbuilding text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and modifiers (' and', ' dynamic', ' like', 'going', ' a') in abstract technical or academic prose, where a noun or modifier is expected next. Peaks are mixed and the evidence is weak and inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on commas and conjunctions (and/or) separating items in a list of third-person verb phrases, like "promotes innovation, enhances X, and provides...". Predicts another verb such as allows, helps, increases. Silent on commas after other clause types.
result.label: Comma in verb-phrase lists

result.description: Fires mid-word on a word-piece such as 'ing' in "contingent/contingency" (also 'tr', 'per', some function words), where the word is unfinished and a suffix like -ent/-ency follows. Silent on 'ing' as a verb suffix in design-ing, model-ing.
result.label: Mid-word 'ing' in 'contingent'

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (apostrophe, 'the', 'of', 'a', word pieces) in formal expository prose about history, politics and institutions. Peaks are inconsistent; the apostrophe is silent after names like Plan or William. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository history prose

result.description: Fires on words that introduce a list of examples after a general noun, mainly "such as", "from", "like", and sometimes commas. It stays quiet on "as well as" and causal "as".
result.label: Example-introducing "such as" / "from"

result.description: Fires on the closing parenthesis after an abbreviation or term in parentheses, such as "(DFS)" or "(RCSA)", typically a sentence subject, and pushes the next token toward a verb like "is".
result.label: Closing paren after parenthetical acronym

result.description: Fires on the 'ates' piece completing "plates" in tectonic/geology text (pl+ates). It stays silent on 'ates' ending verbs like originates, investigates, delineates.
result.label: 'ates' in "plates" (tectonics)

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment ' ren' (mostly in "renormalization") where the next piece is expected to complete a longer word, such as -ormal- or -owned. Weak firing on a few other incomplete word starts like monaster- and sample.
result.label: ' ren' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' the', ',', ' in', 'al', ' classical') in music, arts and education text, where the next word could be music-related. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Music/arts context function words

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, mostly 'ural' in "procedural"/"architectural", plus ' the', ' a', ' programming' in technical or computing text. Silent on 'ural' in "structural". Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Technical text 'ural' and function words

result.description: Fires on ' also' right after "but" in the "not only X but also Y" construction, typically in abstract academic prose. It stays quiet on other uses of ' also', such as after a subject or modal verb, or at the start of a text.
result.label: 'but also' in 'not only…but also'

result.description: Fires on ' be' as a sentence-initial imperative after a comma or clause ("be sure to", "be mindful", "be relevant"). Silent on ' be' after "to", "don't" or "'ll". Also fires on 'be' as a word-start piece.
result.label: Imperative ' be' after comma

result.description: Fires on the plural noun object (disciplines, practices, techniques, concepts, subjects) right after a verb of merging or combining, such as "merge", "meld", "fuse" or "converge". It stays silent on "disciplines" when no merging verb precedes it.
result.label: Objects of merging/blending verbs

result.description: Fires on plural nouns like "examples", "studies", "scenarios" that head a phrase presenting illustrative case material (e.g. "real-life examples of", "case studies"), in section overviews introducing case studies. Silent in other illustrate contexts.
result.label: Illustrative examples/case studies nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also 'for', 'of') after a preposition like "in", "across", "part of" when a field or domain noun is expected next (e.g. "in the culinary field"). Often silent on 'the' elsewhere. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: 'the' after preposition before field noun

result.description: Fires mostly on ' in' (also ' across', ' shape', ' effective') after abstract nouns or verbs in essay-style text about communication, technology and management, e.g. "communication management in". Silent on ' in' after "roles in" or "phase in".
result.label: ' in' after communication-management nouns

result.description: Fires on the verb "keeping"/"Keep"/"keep" (also the "ing" of "keeping"), mostly in advice or instruction text like "keeping everything clean" or "keeping up with". Members are detectors of keep/stay verbs.
result.label: keep / keeping verb

result.description: Fires on a word stem in the middle of an adverb-to-be (spont-, harmon-, fluid, tempor-) where the next piece is an adverb suffix like -ally, -iously, -ly. Predicts adverb endings.
result.label: Adverb stem awaiting -ally/-ly

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' ancient', ' early', 'ing', 'from') in history-of-transportation and technology text, where the next word is likely an era term like "ancient" or "primitive". Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is weak.
result.label: Historical-origins transport/technology context

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' these', ' in', 'al', ' that') inside text about grammar, demonstratives and language or math explanations. It is inconsistent and silent on many ' these' cases, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in grammar text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word endings (' the', 'ing', ',', ' social') in academic or technical expository text, mid-phrase where a continuation is expected. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' the' is silent after "of the" in some contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered function-word or suffix tokens ('ed', ' and', ',', ' even') in explanatory text about chemistry reactions or art technique, mid-phrase before a descriptive word. The peak token is inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed connectives in chemistry/art prose

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece ' bre' before 'eding' (selective/precision breeding), with weaker hits on 'osc' in chiaroscuro, ' long', and a sentence-initial ' In'. Mixed peaks; mainly a ' bre' word-piece detector.
result.label: ' bre' in breeding (mixed)

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: a bare ' ' before a number (e.g. in date or time ranges), ' invol' in "involvement", and some function words. It stays silent on ' ' before century numbers after "the". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Space before number, ' invol'

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'at' in "versatility" (also chromatographic, other word fragments like 'esian', ' ins'), where the word is incomplete and likely continues with 'ility'. Silent on ordinary whole-word text.
result.label: 'at' inside versatility-like words

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', ' of', ' a') after "lack of awareness/understanding of/about" and similar abstract phrases in philosophical or psychological prose. Silent on many ' the' tokens in similar text, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in abstract philosophical prose

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (the, of, connect, known, commas) in expository academic text where a noun is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens before noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' nan' (or ' Nan') that begins nano- words such as nanomaterials, nanotechnology and nanometer, in materials-science text. It predicts continuations like 'ote', 'ometer' and 'osc'.
result.label: ' nan' nano- prefix

result.description: Fires on nouns of development or change (evolution, advancement, progression, progress, expansion) as the head of a phrase in abstract essay-style text, typically after adjectives like "continuous" or "incessant". Silent on "evolutionary".
result.label: Evolution/advancement/progress nouns

result.description: Fires on the subject noun or pronoun (our sentences, we, nuclear reactors, companies) in "without X / to prevent X" clauses, just before a predicted "would/could" or a negative outcome. Peak tokens vary; it tracks the subject slot.
result.label: Subject before hypothetical "would" outcome

result.description: Fires on the word piece " advoc" (advocates/advocated/advocating), strongest after an "-ism" subject such as Existentialism or Conservatism. Silent when it begins a document or sentence with no preceding subject.
result.label: ' advoc' after an ism subject

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: ' into' after divide/subdivide, word-start pieces like ' Des', ' Dem', 'itive', and some commas, mostly in sampling or business/academic text. Peaks are scattered with low consistency; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered word pieces and 'into' after dividing

result.description: Fires on ' is' (sometimes ' are') right after a bare singular subject noun with no article, like "array is" or "set is", at the start of a definition. Predicts descriptive continuations such as "made up of" or "composed of". Silent in some other 'is' contexts.
result.label: ' is' after bare subject noun

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' jo' in "joke" (after "a" or "clever"), predicting the continuation piece like 'ke'. Weak activations on other word-start fragments such as 'Rob' in "Robuchon" and 'plot'.
result.label: ' jo' piece before 'ke' (joke)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "clar" when it begins a word like "clarification" (as in "clarification needed" tags). It is mostly silent elsewhere, with rare weak firing on "ment" in Enlightenment.
result.label: "clar" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments that begin a longer word, mainly 'qui' in "inquiries", also 'genu', 'utter', 'ig'. It is a word-piece completion latent, with members detecting partial word pieces such as qui, rever, increment, indust.
result.label: Mid-word piece 'qui' in inquiries

result.description: Fires on the hyphen after a word like "one-of", "next", "state-of" or "first" in fixed compound phrases (one-of-a-kind, next-generation), predicting a specific continuation. Stays silent on hyphens after "-based" style modifiers (agent-, CRISPR-, real-).
result.label: Hyphen in fixed compounds (one-of-a-kind)

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'ative', ' enthus', ' and', dashes) inside lists or noun phrases naming groups of people or professions, such as 'chefs and food enthusiasts'. It pushes toward person-noun endings like -ular, developers, people, children. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Person-group noun phrase continuation

result.description: Fires on "ancient" (mostly the piece "cient" in "Ancient" and the word " ancient"), especially in lists of ancient civilizations. Members are detectors of this token, and the logits favor next words about ancient peoples and places, such as Greek and Egypt.
result.label: "ancient" token, ancient civilizations

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' in', ' when', ' an', '4', ' s') in technical expository text, mid-phrase where a technical noun or modifier is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse and weakly faithful.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase function words, technical text

result.description: Fires on ' electron'/' electrons' and function words (of, the, each) right before a particle or physics term, in physics and chemistry text on bound states and quantum particles. It stays silent on ' electron' in atomic-configuration contexts.
result.label: Electron / physics-particle slot

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly verbs like " adapt", " manifest", " interpret", plus " and" in "nuances and complexities", in abstract academic prose about language and linguistics. Peaks are mixed and weakly consistent; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Abstract linguistics prose, verbs like adapt

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ographic' in "Biogeographic" (especially at the start of a document or heading), and weakly in other -ographic/-istic word endings. It stays silent on 'ographic' in "geographic isolation".
result.label: Biogeographic 'ographic' suffix

result.description: Fires on the 'K' token in "Al-Khwarizmi" (the K after "Al-"), predicting the continuation "hw…". Weaker on other K-initial name pieces like Runge-Kutta and Kesh.
result.label: K in Al-Khwarizmi

result.description: Fires on nominalization suffixes or process nouns (-lication, -ization, -ulation, -ement, validation, integration) ending a technical process term in computing/engineering text. Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Technical process-noun suffixes

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ot' in "Robot(ics)" at the start of a document or heading, and on ' increasing' before an '-ly' ending (becoming increasingly). Silent on 'ot' in "promoters". The two triggers look unrelated.
result.label: Robot 'ot' and 'increasing(ly)'

result.description: Fires on clause-introducing conjunctions such as " that" and " because" (also " since", colons) after a verb or noun, where a full clause follows, mostly in abstract academic or explanatory prose. Predicts a clause subject like "all", "there", "it".
result.label: Clause-introducing 'that'/'because' connectives

result.description: Fires on words about thriving or flourishing (thrive, prosper, growth, success, longevity, viability, competitive), often in business or institutional text about continued success. Peaks vary across several word pieces.
result.label: Thriving, prosperity, success words

result.description: Fires on ideology suffixes (-ist, -istic, -ial, -ism) completing words like nationalist, communist, anti-colonial in political/historical text, especially after "national". Silent when "ist" starts a text with no such stem. Pushes toward sentiment/interests.
result.label: Political -ist/-istic suffix after nation

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix 'ic' in "catastrophic" (and similar negative-adjective stems), plus a few appositive/definition function words like ' a', ' or', ' essentially'. Silent on 'ic' in other words such as strategic or economic. Weak, mixed circuit.
result.label: 'ic' in catastrophic

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on mixed tokens (' and', ' motiv', 'ative', ' Nor', '/') in expository text about language, writing and literature, often mid-word or at a connector. Silent on many ' and' in narrative/character discussions. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Mixed connectors in language-topic prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece " strateg" (strategies/strategists) when it follows a modifying noun, such as "marketing strategies" or "survival strategies". It stays silent when the piece starts a sentence or is followed by "strategic" as in "strategic planning".
result.label: ' strateg' after modifier noun
Example-introducers after metrics/measures
result.description: Fires on "such as", "include", "including", "like" that introduce a list of examples, most strongly after nouns about metrics or measurements (e.g. "metrics include", "quantitative aspects such as"). It stays silent on "such as" after other kinds of nouns.

Fires on plural nouns naming analytical or testing methods (" tests", "analyses", " analysis") in scientific or materials-science lists of techniques, e.g. "mechanical tests including...", "thermal analyses such as...". Predicts a following list of methods.
result.label: Scientific test/analysis method nouns

result.description: Fires on the comma or "is" right after "instance" or "example" (e.g. "For instance," / "One example is"), where an illustration is about to be introduced. Silent on ordinary commas elsewhere.
result.label: Comma/is after "instance"/"example"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (century, form, stages, -ical, in, the) in abstract, academic descriptions of cultural or intellectual history and movements. Peaks are scattered and the contrast shows it silent on some 'century' cases, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Abstract cultural-history phrasing, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on ' Cir' (and sometimes ' Begin') as the first token of a heading-like line at or near document start, e.g. a list of topic headings like "Polygons. Circles." It stays silent on mid-sentence mentions of circles.
result.label: ' Cir' starting a heading line

result.description: Fires mainly on ' partially' (also 'only', 'completely', 'not') in chemistry text about weak versus strong acids and bases dissociating or ionizing only partly. Members are acid/base and chemistry topic detectors.
result.label: Partial dissociation of weak acids/bases

result.description: Fires on " the" after a verb or conjunction like "embracing", "and", "reflecting" or "emphasized", where an abstract noun (spirit, desire, exploration) follows in art or history prose. Silent on " the" after sentence-opening prepositions such as "In" or "During".
result.label: "the" before abstract cultural nouns

result.description: Fires on prepositions (mostly " in", also on/within/at) right after "ensure/ensuring performance/stability/safety", introducing the setting or conditions ("even in the face of", "in real-world"). Silent on "in" in other uses like "in part" or "in terms of".
result.label: Preposition after ensuring/maintaining performance

result.description: Fires on ' cell', ' energy' and similar word pieces in biology/lipid text where the next word is likely an adjective-like continuation (cellular, architecture). Silent on some ' cell' tokens in other contexts, so the needed context is unclear.
result.label: Cell/energy before cellular continuation

result.description: Fires on the token ' I' when it starts a word or acronym such as "Ion", "Ionization", "ISA", or a Roman numeral, rather than the pronoun. It mostly fires at the start of a document or heading, and the next piece is often a word continuation.
result.label: ' I' as word-initial fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' be', ' in', ' will', ' means', ' value') in statistics/probability explanations, e.g. the Law of Large Numbers. It is silent on ' be' in other statistical passages, so the conditions are unclear.
result.label: Function words in probability explanations

result.description: Fires on a determiner or quantifier (' a', ' the', ' more', ' greater') right after "allows/allowed/allowing for", where the next word is an abstract capability noun like flexibility or freedom. Silent on ' a' after other prepositions.
result.label: Determiner after "allows for"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' invas' (as in "invasive species"), predicting a continuation like 'ive'. Members are mostly detectors of ' invas' and other incomplete word-start fragments.
result.label: ' invas' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of place names (states, countries, cities), as in "Paris, New York City" or "Norway, Denmark, Finland". Silent on commas in ordinary clause or phrase boundaries.
result.label: Commas in place-name lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'os' inside "monosaccharides" (after "mon"), and weakly on similar mid-word pieces like 'lig'. It stays silent on 'os' in other words such as ribosomes, chaos, ratios.
result.label: 'os' in monosaccharides

result.description: Fires on the 'quest' piece of "Norman Conquest" (and occasionally the year digits after it), in text about English language history. Silent in some post-Norman "Conquest" contexts, so the exact conditions are unclear.
result.label: Norman Conquest 'quest' token

result.description: Fires on nouns for a chemical or thermodynamic process (' equilibrium', ' reaction', ' process', ' system') in chemistry and thermodynamics text, e.g. Gibbs free energy and reaction shifts. Silent on one 'chemical equilibrium' example.
result.label: Chemical process nouns (equilibrium, reaction)

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start pieces like ' conver' (converge/convergent) and ' orn' (ornamental), where the word continues with a suffix. Predicts continuations like 'gent', 'ging', 'amental'. Silent on the complete word 'convergence'.
result.label: Word-start fragment 'conver'/'orn'

result.description: Fires on abstract head nouns ending a noun phrase in academic text (process, landscape, ecosystem, methodology, domain, level), where a modifier precedes. Silent on 'process' used mid-phrase or as a verb.
result.label: Abstract system/domain noun ending phrase

result.description: Fires on contrastive conjunctions (' but', ' however', ' although', ' yet') that follow a clause stating something, mainly in descriptive or historical prose, where a qualifying or opposing clause comes next. Silent on 'not X but Y' style.
result.label: Contrastive 'but/however' after a clause

result.description: Fires on verbs of supplying or giving, such as provide, providing, provides and offer, especially when an abstract subject (a method, tool or concept) supplies something like insight, a formula or a platform. Mostly in analytical or mathematical text.
result.label: provide/offer verbs with abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the last token of a multi-word theory or concept name from social science and management, such as "Power distance", "Hierarchy of Needs" and "Power distance index". Mixed peak tokens, weak consistency. Silent on "ance" in unrelated words.
result.label: Social-science theory term endings

result.description: Fires on place names (countries, cities, states) right after the preposition "in" that locate something, e.g. "in Paris", "in southern France", "in Liverpool". Silent when the name is not a location after "in", like "nation-states like France".
result.label: Place name after "in"

result.description: Fires on verbs and verb-like pieces (processes, handles, stores, -ing) that follow a subject or "that/it" and describe what a system or component does with events or data. Silent when "processes" is a plural noun.
result.label: Verb slot after system subject

result.description: Fires on singular person or kin nouns (child, brother, owner, person, friend, girl) after a determiner or "one"/"her"/"my", often in examples about a generic individual. Predicts continuations like who, else, -hood or -mate.
result.label: Singular person/kin noun after determiner

result.description: Fires on the word "speech" (or its piece "ech" in "Speech") as a noun for spoken language or speaking, such as speech structure, speech therapy, direct speech and speeches. It predicts follow-ups like -es, patterns, recognition and acts.
result.label: "speech" token detector

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' Der' (Derrida, Derivative, Derain) and ' Liter' (Literary), occasionally ' hyper'. It marks an incomplete word start that is continued by a suffix piece such as 'r', 'iv' or 'ary'.
result.label: Der-/Liter- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the word " mass" (or "Mass") in physics and chemistry text, such as relativistic mass, atomic mass, rest mass and mass analysis. Members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token.
result.label: Word "mass" in science text

result.description: Fires mostly on digits like '9', '8', '7' in number sequences or lists (times, series of numbers), with scattered weaker firing on function words. Silent on '9' inside a year like 1905. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Digits in number sequences

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' flav' (start of flavor/flavors) in food and cooking text, predicting completions like 'or', 'ors', 'our'. Silent when it starts the document with no preceding context.
result.label: ' flav' word-piece before -or/-ors

result.description: Fires on shape or form adjectives and word pieces (curved, flat, smooth, straight, -onal, -ine) in geometry or physical-shape descriptions, where a noun like "shapes", "edges" or "surfaces" is likely next.
result.label: Shape-describing adjectives (curved, flat, smooth)

result.description: Fires on scattered, unrelated tokens: 'process', the 'icing' piece of "Pricing", ' eastern' and ' cold' in climate (La Niña) text. No single meaning is clear; peaks are inconsistent and the members are mostly generic.
result.label: Mixed tokens: process, icing, eastern

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' rel' when it starts a longer word (relentless, relays, relatability, relational), predicting a continuation like 'ent', 'ays' or 'ational'. It stays silent when ' rel' is at the very start of the text.
result.label: ' rel' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on ' to' (or ' until') as the endpoint marker in a "from X to Y" time-range, especially after a year or century (e.g. "from 1750 to 19…"). Silent on ordinary 'to' such as "relating to" or "leading to".
result.label: 'to' ending a date range

result.description: Fires on possessive determiners (mostly " their") right after verbs like showcase, demonstrate or display, where a noun for abilities or qualities (skills, talent) comes next. It stays quiet on " their" after prepositions or conjunctions.
result.label: Their after showcase/display verbs

result.description: Fires on the 'ing' piece inside the word "contingent" (cont-ing-ent), in philosophical text about necessity. Weaker on 'il' in "resilient". Silent on ordinary '-ing' verb endings.
result.label: 'ing' inside "contingent"

result.description: Fires on plural-subject copula ' are' (also 'being', 'were') after a plural noun subject in academic-style text, where a predicate like 'increasingly/also/now becoming' follows. Silent on some 'are' cases, e.g. after 'that' or certain subjects.
result.label: plural noun subject + 'are'

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces of geometry terms (rect, tri, squ, circum) that precede "-angle/-angular/-ference", mainly in lists of shapes in geometry text. Predicts "angular"/"angle". Silent on "Latin rect-" outside geometry.
result.label: Geometry word-start pieces (rect, tri)

result.description: Fires on ' won' (mostly in "won't" contractions) and on ' the' after "of"/"to" in abstract academic phrasing, plus a few other tokens. Mixed peaks; evidence is thin and the circuit fits poorly.
result.label: ' won' contraction and ' the'

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'con' (also ' Con') at the start of a longer word, such as mis-con-ceptions, super-con-ductivity, con-junction. Predicts continuations like 'cept', 'vent', 'duct', 'vers'.
result.label: 'con' word-piece prefix

result.description: Fires on the word " settlement" (human settlement, rural or ethnic settlement patterns) in academic social-science text, and predicts "patterns", "sites", "districts" next. Members are mostly settlement detectors plus related abstract-noun detectors.
result.label: ' settlement' noun, settlement patterns

result.description: Fires on the word " community" when it is used as a modifier before a following noun, as in "community participation", "community growth" or "community building". It predicts words like spirit, involvement, participation, pride.
result.label: ' community' as noun modifier

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Hyp" (before "othesis") in lists of named hypotheses, such as the Input Hypothesis or Monitor Hypothesis. It also fires weakly on other split-word starts like Pre.
result.label: " Hyp" start of "Hypothesis" names

result.description: Fires on the "-ates" ending of "necessitates" (also "necessitated"/"necessitating"), where the verb means "requires". It is silent on "ates" in other words like "integrates" or "vertebrates". Predicts words like careful, thorough, strict.
result.label: necessitates (requires) verb ending

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ra' when it begins a longer word, such as "cooling ra|cks", "ra|infall" or "ra|ises". The strongest case is "cooling rack". It predicts word continuations like 'inf', 'ref', 'cks'.
result.label: ' ra' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start pieces like ' mob' (mobility), ' occurr' (occurring), ' behav' (behaviors), ' symmet', where the next token completes the word with a suffix such as 'ility' or 'iors'. Silent on ' mob' at document start.
result.label: Word-start fragments awaiting suffix

result.description: Fires on the token "linear", most strongly as the piece after "Non" or "non-" (Nonlinear Dynamics/Regression), and also on " linear" in math text. Predicts continuations like "ity", "dynamics" and "differential".
result.label: "linear" in nonlinear/math contexts

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' eth' (and ' Eth') that starts words like ethical, ethics, ethos, and also ethers. It predicts continuations such as 'ical' and 'os'. Members are mostly ' eth' detectors.
result.label: ' eth' word-start token

result.description: Fires on the token " nature", most strongly after adjectives like "dynamic", "evolving" or "intricate" in the phrase "ADJ nature of X". It predicts " of" next. Many members are plain " nature" detectors.
result.label: ' nature' after adjective

result.description: Fires on "reduction"/"reducing" (including pieces like redu|ction), mainly in chemistry redox contexts (reduction reactions, reducing agents), and weakly on "redox". Predicts "agent(s)" or "potential" next.
result.label: Reduction (chemical redox sense)

result.description: Fires on word pieces 'ult' (in socioc-ult-ural, interc-ult-ural) and 'switch' (code-switch-ing) in sociolinguistics text, predicting suffix continuations like 'ural'. Weaker on 'depth' and 'effects'.
result.label: 'ult' in sociocultural, code-'switch'

result.description: Fires on the prefix token ' un' when it begins a word like unfamiliar, uncharted or unexamined, usually after a preposition or verb such as "into" or "through". It pushes toward continuations like 'famil', 'pre' and 'chart'.
result.label: ' un' word-prefix after preposition

result.description: Fires on connectors (mostly ' and') right after "stable" or "stability" in economic/system-stability text, e.g. "stable and predictable", "stability and control". It stays quiet on ' and' ending ordinary lists of factors.
result.label: 'and' after stability/stable

result.description: Fires on the word piece " techn" when it starts "technological", especially after "factors such as", "due to", "influenced by", where a list of causes is expected. Silent on " techn" after "new" or "manufacturing" (techn-ologies as a product).
result.label: techn(ological) as a cause factor

result.description: Fires on the word "distributed" (and the piece "ributed" in "Distributed"), mostly in computing contexts like distributed systems, computing, databases. Predicts nouns like environments, systems, computing. Also fires weakly on "parallel" and "consensus".
result.label: "distributed" in computing

result.description: Fires on the word piece " master"/" Master" when it begins a word like mastering, mastery, masterpiece, predicting suffixes such as -ing, -y, -fully. Silent on "master of" used as a standalone noun.
result.label: master- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on adjectives like " explicit" and " literal" (also "fancy", "particular") that modify a noun about meaning or communication, such as explicit signals or literal meaning. It's backed by explicit/implicit, direct/clear and formal detectors.
result.label: explicit / literal meaning adjectives

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside art-technique terms in lists of drawing/painting techniques (Shading, Stippling, Sfumato, Impasto). Silent on lists of people's names. Members are art/painting detectors.
result.label: Art technique term pieces

result.description: Fires on word endings that close mathematical/physics field names or terms (cohomology, renormalization, algebras, String Theory), where a noun like "group" or "theory" may follow. Silent on "ology" in biology and ethnomusicology.
result.label: Math/physics term-ending suffixes

result.description: Fires on scattered function-like tokens (blank space tokens, ' yet', ' that', word pieces) mid-phrase in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent, with no dominant token; logits weakly favor verbs like 'seek' or 'find'.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " cor" (as in corrosion, coral) before the rest of the word is seen. It predicts continuation pieces like "rosion" or "al". Members are mostly " cor" token detectors.
result.label: ' cor' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' completing "empir-ical" (also 'experimental'), mostly before words like evidence, observation, verification. Silent on 'ical' in other words such as philosophical or Classical. Predicts evidence/proof/truth.
result.label: empirical (-ical after empir-)

result.description: Fires on the token "made" in the compound "human-made" / "man-made" / "hand-made", where it ends a hyphenated artificial-origin modifier before a noun like features or structures. Members detect artificial, natural, and -ed/-made word pieces.
result.label: hyphenated "-made" (man-made)

result.description: Fires on a comma, "and", or "denotes" right after the abstract quality noun "clarity" (or similar quality words like "concise") in lists of communication virtues. It is silent on commas after other nouns in similar lists.
result.label: Comma/and after "clarity" in lists

result.description: Fires on commas and "and" that separate items in a list of abstract process or property nouns (flow, movement, quality; acquisition, processing), where another list item is expected. Silent on commas that start a participle clause.
result.label: List separators after process nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'avel' in "w|avel|ength(s)", after a preceding 'w' piece. Weak on similar mid-word pieces (w-ard-robe, stain-less). Silent when 'avel' starts the text without the 'w'.
result.label: 'avel' inside wavelength

result.description: Fires on the word " tax" (also " Tax") when it follows a modifier or context word in taxation text, e.g. "better tax benefits", "effective tax planning". It is silent on a sentence-initial "tax-and-". Members are tax-token detectors.
result.label: ' tax' token after modifier

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'oth' (sloth), 'elt' (Celtic), 'ber' (strawberries) and 'enz', where the word is still incomplete. It is often in food or list contexts. Logits suggest suffix pieces come next (ts, os, horn). Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-word fragments oth/elt/ber

result.description: Fires on the word " virtue" (and pieces like "ue"/"ues" in "virtues"), mostly in virtue ethics contexts. It predicts continuations like " eth" (ethics). Upstream members are mostly virtue-token detectors.
result.label: virtue token (virtue ethics)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'brid' in "hybrid"/"hybridization", mostly in chemical bonding text. It predicts suffixes like 'ization' and 'ized'. It stays silent when 'brid' starts the text with no 'hy' before it.
result.label: 'brid' in hybrid(ization)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "wh" (as in who/whom/whose/whisk) when it begins a word and is split off as its own token. It pushes toward completions like -ether, -atever, -ilst and -ose.
result.label: word-initial "wh" piece

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (where, when, or, of, in) in text defining or explaining economic externalities and market failure. It seems to predict an upcoming "third (parties)" or "external" continuation. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low.
result.label: Connectors in externalities explanations

result.description: Fires on abstract academic nouns like theory, principles, techniques, concepts ending a noun phrase in historical passages about the foundations of mathematics or knowledge. It stays quiet on 'theory' in other phrases, such as 'probability theory'. Predicts a following clause with temporal words.
result.label: Abstract field nouns in historical foundations

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: ' in' after "established/took place" before a year, ' treated', 'est' in "aesthetic", list commas. Silent on ' in' after nouns like "changes in". Evidence is mixed and the peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: Mixed ' in' before years, scattered tokens
